title: MZ How to make a deployed game's folder look cleaner?

posts.author: Hamoody
posts.body:
I really hope this is the right forum for this but basicallywhen I deploy a RPG Maker MZ project, the folder contains the .exe file but there's other files like "icudtl.dat", "notification_helper.exe" and "v8_context_snapshot.bin" etc.
Is there a way to delete these files or move them somewhere else? So the main folder will only game game.exe, index.html and package.json?

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
NW Package and/or VM​
I bookmarked this a while ago, but haven't actually tried it yet:
How to package and distribute your apps
Call all Node.js modules directly from DOM/WebWorker and enable a new way of writing applications with all Web technologies. - nwjs/nw.js
github.com
With this approach you might need a plugin to change the location of the
save
folder. (I imagine that after packaging,
process.mainModule.filename
would point to an address in the new executable, causing an error when attempting to save.)
Note that the last part, about how to minimise file count on Windows, mentions Enigma Virtual Box. Running your game through a virtual machine will create additional overhead and is not recommended if you want to minimise frame drops on lower-end systems.
Tree structure​
Alternatively you could ship the files in this kind of directory structure to make things look neater:
Launcher
files
game.exe
,
icudtl.dat
, etc.
There are various options for the "launcher", e.g. (for Windows):
Batch file (
launcher.bat
):
Code:
cd files
game.exe
Relative link (
launcher.lnk
):
https://superuser.com/a/644421
A precompiled app (
launcher.exe
).
You might be able to find a general-purpose launcher app for this?
This option is mainly useful for pre-launch config rather than acting as a relay.
